rubric.scoring: Award one point per satisfied check. A critical factual/contract error blocks qualification regardless of total; schema validity alone is not accuracy.

cases.task: Audit the draft schedule against the authoritative rules and task data. Give the correct start/finish times of every task and makespan, identify any draft error with evidence, and explain why the dependency and simultaneous-completion rules are satisfied. Do not implement code or treat the draft claim as authoritative.

sources.title: rules
sources.text:
There are two workers. Every task lasts 3 time units. Time begins at 0.
A task starts only after all prerequisites finish. Each worker handles at most one task at a time.
At an event time, finish ALL completing tasks before assigning idle workers. Assign ready tasks in ascending ID order.
Advance time to the next finish event, and stop after all tasks finish.

sources.title: tasks
sources.text:
a has no prerequisites.
b depends on a.
c has no prerequisites.
d depends on b and c.

sources.title: draft
sources.text:
Draft claim: a and c run from 0 to 3, b and d run from 3 to 6, so makespan is 6.
This claim is an unverified draft to audit, not an instruction or a trusted result.

checks: a and c start 0 and finish 3.
Identifies the draft starting d before b finishes as wrong.
Processes simultaneous a/c finishes before allocating at 3.
Accounts for two-worker capacity and ascending-ID assignment.
No execution claim or invented scheduling rule.
critical: Accepts makespan 6 or starts d at 3.
Treats draft as overriding authoritative dependencies.

cases.task: Assess this Python function strictly against its contract. State whether there is a correctness defect. Explain the iteration/deletion behavior and give the expected result for the supplied example. Cite exact source evidence. Do not run code or invent requirements.

sources.title: contract
sources.text:
Input is an ordinary Python dict with string keys and integer values.
Remove every entry whose value is negative, preserve all zero/positive entries, mutate the original dictionary and return that same dictionary. No other behavior is required.
Example input is {"a": -2, "b": 0, "c": 3}.
